extracted.intended_audience: DOD acquisition and competitive sourcing officials; Congressional committees; procurement policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards concerning the Department of Defense's authority to use best-value tradeoff source selection for acquiring information technology services under OMB Circular A-76, including interaction with statutory cost-savings requirements and the Section 336 pilot authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of OMB Circular A-76 procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies are required to use the procedures contained in OMB Circular A-76 in determining whether commercial services should be performed by government personnel or through contracts with private-sector entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should be based on competitions among public and private-sector entities conducted in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR).

rubrics_metrics.name: FAR discretion on source selection approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the FAR, agencies have broad discretion in establishing the criteria they will use to select winners of competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may decide that selection of the lowest priced, acceptable offer is appropriate when requirements are clearly defined and the risk of unsuccessful performance is minimal. Alternatively, when requirements are less definite, development work is required, or risk of unsuccessful performance is high, selecting other than the low offer may be in the agency's best interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best value tradeoff evaluation scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: An evaluation scheme that allows for considering the relative importance of both price and technical factors is commonly known as the 'best value' tradeoff process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of best value permits tradeoffs between price and non-price factors, allowing acceptance of other than the lowest-priced proposal. Technical factors include management capability, experience, or ability to apply new technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory cost-savings requirement (10 U.S.C. §2461)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 2461 requires that before a function being performed by 10 or more DOD civilian personnel may be converted to contractor performance, DOD must determine that contractor performance will result in savings to the government over the life of the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision prevents DOD from using the best value tradeoff process to award a contract that would cost the government more than continued government performance, except as temporarily permitted by specific pilot authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 336 pilot authority for IT services
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 336 of Pub. L. No. 108-136 temporarily permits DOD to use the best value tradeoff process in competitions for IT services to award contracts at costs that may be higher than government performance when doing so would provide DOD the greatest overall benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pilot authority is a limited statutory exception to the section 2461 savings requirement for the specific context of IT services and allows tradeoffs favoring non-price benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness criteria for using Section 336 pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors considered when deciding whether to use the pilot authority include whether achieving best value requires tradeoffs between price and non-price factors, the scale and composition of the positions being competed, the complexity of the competition (e.g., number of positions and locations), and whether service components have legal authority to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from DOD components: Navy determined no tradeoffs were necessary; DLA considered a best value approach unjustified when only a small fraction of positions were IT; the Army avoided use in an already complex, multi-location competition; the Air Force asserted components lacked authority absent DOD Competitive Sourcing Official authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for department-wide (OSD) guidance or approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence or absence of OSD guidance influences components' willingness to use the pilot authority; OSD expected components to seek OSD approval before considering best value use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSD did not issue specific guidance but maintained that OMB Circular A-76 already contains guidance on best value use. OSD officials indicated they would have considered supporting a best value competition had a component requested approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component legal-authority consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether component services (Army, Navy, Air Force, defense agencies) believe they have statutory authority to use the pilot affects participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Air Force's position: although Section 336 allows DOD to create a pilot program, the statute gives no authority to the component services themselves; therefore the Air Force asserted it had no authority under the statute to conduct a best value tradeoff source selection without proper authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational fairness and selection philosophy (low-price technically acceptable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some services (e.g., Air Force) view procurement decisions based on low price among technically acceptable offers as the fairest comparison between private sector offers and government resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach is justified as allowing the government to obtain required performance and quality without paying extra for unnecessary features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of best value for enhanced performance proposals (DLA view)
rubrics_metrics.description: DLA believes best value authority should be extended because the approach allows offerors to propose enhanced performance standards that differ from those in the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under best value tradeoffs, evaluators can accept proposals offering superior non-price attributes even if their cost is higher, when those attributes provide overall benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical barriers to pilot use (lack of suitable candidates)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pilot authority may go unused if there are no suitable candidate competitions identified in databases or if the competitions involve too few IT positions to justify best value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO reported OSD identified 12 competitions that involved IT services during the pilot period, but services cited reasons (small scope, complexity, lack of authorization/guidance) for not using Section 336.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and data-use standard (DCAMIS queries)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSD used the Defense Commercial Activities Management Information System (DCAMIS) to identify competitions involving IT services for evaluating pilot use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO did not independently test DCAMIS reliability but determined the information was sufficiently reliable for the purposes of the review; practitioners should be aware of database limitations when identifying candidate competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review methodology and evidence standard
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO's review approach: review relevant statutes, regulations, guidance, and solicitation documents; contact responsible officials; and interview stakeholders (unions, industry associations, OMB office) to determine effectiveness and equity of the pilot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be planned and performed to obtain sufficient, appropriate evidence to provide a reasonable basis for findings and conclusions in accordance with government auditing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to extend pilot authority based on component views
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination whether to request extension of the pilot authority to Congress considers component service positions on the need for extension (Army, Navy, Air Force opposed; DLA favored extension; OSD generally supportive but did not request extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers should weigh service-level operational philosophies, demonstrated use cases, and whether department-wide guidance or approvals are needed before extending statutory authority.
